what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force appointed Tim Wilmer as chair by voice vote, reorganizing after a long gap.
The vice chair election was postponed until the absent member's interest is known.
The DPW described tracking stormwater labor, equipment and hours monthly, with all stormwater funding now coming from the DPW budget.
Members discussed a stormwater utility enterprise fund, including starting at current spending and a rough per-household charge; nothing was decided.

why_it_matters: Stormwater work is paid from the DPW budget today, so a separate enterprise fund would move that cost onto a per-household charge that residents could be asked to accept.
Rising drainage spending and storm cleanup costs are the mechanism pushing the town toward that choice; no charge or fund size has been set.

meetings.headline: Stormwater Task Force tabled its reorganization to August and heard ARPA money is unlikely for stormwater projects.
meetings.summary: The task force tabled reorganization until the August meeting, approved the prior minutes, and heard that the town manager showed little interest in using ARPA funds for stormwater. Most of the meeting was a briefing on failing detention basins at the Village of Flat Hill development and the town's possible role, plus a discussion of silt and bank erosion on the Malpas Brook near Hickory Hills. The next meeting was set for August 17 and the meeting adjourned.
